title: StitchScope Stitch Recipe (non-photo, generic construction)
description: The structured shape a NON-PHOTO recipe call must conform to: how a named stitch family is conventionally constructed, as concrete steps -- never an absolute foundation chain count for any specific swatch size. Produced by engine/vision.py's get_stitch_recipe(), a separate API call with no image attached, asked generically ('how is X conventionally constructed') rather than grounded in a photo -- the same model invents garment-specific numbers when a photo call is asked to propose row structure, but gives correct, standard answers to this generic framing. setup is the one-time steps worked before row 1's repeat starts; repeat is the unit that repeats across a row; turning_chain is the conventional turning-chain steps worked at the start of every row after the first, before that row's repeat starts. engine/schema.py's validate_recipe() enforces these same rules in plain Python.

setup.description: One-time steps worked into the foundation chain before row 1's repeat starts. Can be empty if this stitch needs none.

repeat.description: The unit that repeats across a row. Never empty.

turning_chain.description: Conventional turning-chain steps worked at the start of every row after the first, before that row's repeat starts. Can be empty if this stitch needs no turning chain.
